messages:
alex: starting a thread to lock down the long-context / context-mix benchmark protocol. goal: reproducible apples-to-apples across kernel variants and batching heuristics. short proposal below, want quick thumbs before I write the doc.

maria: +1. want the experiment to make prefill-dominant behavior explicit (we saw big KV cache effects last time).

kevin: agree. can we include a synthetic replay mode and a pure synthetic generator? they stress different code paths.

alex: yep. propose 3 load drivers: (1) replay harness (real traffic traces, same seeds), (2) parametric synthetic (sequence-length and token-rate distributions), (3) prefill-heavy generator (long prefill then short decodes).

nate: important: fixed RNG seeds and same tokenization across runs, otherwise output differences will change batching & KV hits. also pin model version + quantization.

kevin: for kernels we should test: float32 baseline, int8 quantized path, and the new fused-attn path. run each under identical request mixes and collect per-token latency + kernel-level flamegraphs.

alex: benchmark harness outline (rough):
```
- population: N workers (10, 50, 200)
- mixes: long-only (100% seq=8192), mix-A (60% seq=4096, 30% seq=1024, 10% seq=128), prefill-heavy (70% prefill-dominant requests)
- qps targets: 10, 50, 200 (adjust per infra)
- duration: 15m steady-state after 2m ramp
- metrics: p50/p95/p99 token latency, tokens/sec, GPU util, KV hit rate, batching size distribution, kernel time breakdown
```

alex: we also need a deterministic replay format: each trace entry = {seed, prompt-len, decode-len, timestamps} so replay harness can reproduce exact prefill timings.

maria: can we instrument KV cache stats at op granularity? e.g., per-prefill-key hit/miss counts and size of cached KV slices. that helped isolate a regression before.

kevin: add per-batch composition: how many unique prefixes, average KV reuse in batch. that will show batching heuristics' effectiveness.

suzanne: request: include a small synthetic 'regression probe' workload (single long prefill followed by many short decodes) to surface regressions in KV eviction and cache warmup. very sensitive.

loadbot: run queued: longmix-proto-smoke @eng-runtime. will post results to thread when finished. ETA ~20m. :robot_face:

alex: next: profiling hooks. please capture Tracy traces + kernel-level CUPTI timelines on one run, and perf/instr pipeline on CPU for another. keep profile windows aligned with steady-state window.

nate: also capture batching snapshots every 30s (small JSON) with: batch_id, batch_size, sequences_in_batch, kv_reuse_ratio, kernel_variant. store in s3/<exp>/batches.jsonl

maria: validation: run apples-to-apples by swapping kernels only (no config changes). assert delta in p99 token-latency within noise tolerance for non-quantized paths, and flag if >10% regression.

kevin: one more: quantify cost-per-token and cost-per-fulfill (GPU-ms/token, and infra $ estimate). helps tradeoffs.

alex: cool. I'll write the full RFC doc with runbooks + exact CLI commands. quick checklist: deterministic replay format, three drivers, batching snapshots, kv op metrics, profiling plan, regression thresholds, cost calc. any other must-haves?

suzanne: include teardown / cleanup steps for Dedicated pools (to avoid stale reservations).

kevin: annotate expected sensitivity: prefill-heavy -> KV dominated; long-only -> kernel compute dominated; mix-A -> batching heuristics most impactful. put in doc.

alex: thanks. if no objections I'll land a PR to eng-runtime infra repo tonight and kick off a full sweep tomorrow. :+1:
